Application Areas: Cohomology of Arithmetic and Algebraic Groups
Analytic Number Theory and L-function Moments
Connectivity of Classifying Spaces and Geometric Complexes
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Explicit Resolution Construction: Building partial resolutions of length two for Steinberg modules to compute relations among relations and verify vanishing results for codimension-2 rational cohomology in SL_n(Z) for n >= 3.

Homological Stability via Irreducible Representations: Proving stability theorems for discrete groups with coefficients in irreducible algebraic representations, establishing stable ranges independent of polynomial degree to confirm predictions for moments of quadratic L-functions over function fields.

Corrective Homotopy and Filtration Analysis: Rectifying errors in Koszul property proofs by defining rigorous partial orders and filtrations on reduced bar complexes, demonstrating vanishing homology in specific degrees to validate stability results through corrected homotopy arguments.

Geometric Complex Connectivity via Iterated Constructions: Proving connectivity conjectures for the common basis complex by describing it as an iterated bar construction on equivariant monoids derived from Tits buildings, thereby establishing high connectivity for fields and Principal Ideal Domains.
Summary Description: Peter Patzt specializes in algebraic topology and homological algebra, focusing on the cohomology of arithmetic groups, geometric group theory, and algebraic K-theory. His research centers on establishing homological stability for families of discrete groups, particularly General Linear Groups and Symplectic Groups, using coefficients in irreducible algebraic representations and Steinberg modules. Patzt employs explicit partial resolutions, spectral sequences, and combinatorial Morse theory to analyze the connectivity of geometric complexes like Tits buildings and the common basis complex. His work has significant impact in verifying major conjectures, such as the Church–Farb–Putman conjecture and Rognes' connectivity conjecture, and in linking algebraic structures to analytic number theory by confirming predictions for moments of quadratic L-functions over function fields. He is also known for rigorous corrections to foundational proofs regarding Koszul duality and the structure of Steinberg monoids.
